Welcome, humans.  

Robots are _so _back—[Boston Dynamics](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/05/boston-dynamics-joins-forces-with-its-former-ceo-to-speed-the-learning-of-its-atlas-humanoid-robot/), the godfathers of the modern humanoid robot movement, are making some [exciting moves](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/05/boston-dynamics-joins-forces-with-its-former-ceo-to-speed-the-learning-of-its-atlas-humanoid-robot/). The company is teaming up with their former CEO Marc Raibert to make Atlas (the [parkour bot](https://youtu.be/tF4DML7FIWk?feature=shared)) even smarter. 

The partnership with Raibert's [RAI Institute](https://www.responsible.ai/) will focus on making Atlas better at learning through trial and error (reinforcement learning) just like us humans. Think: running faster and lifting heavier things without falling over. 

It’s like hitting the robot gym, except instead of pumping iron to build muscle mass, Atlas will be getting its reps in to build _brain power. _If only our human gym sessions made us smarter instead of just sore!

**Here’s what you need to know about AI today:**

* Google goes all out with releasing Gemini 2.0. 

* Amazon could release genAI Alexa by end of February.

* AI legend Andrej Karpathy dropped an epic AI explainer.

* Researchers found a life-saving treatment for iMCD with AI. 

Advertise in The Neuron here. (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfng1Qz3wGLc_-f9goa1TQgnGE_rehbW55Gx5VaEYIhn4OueQ/viewform)

# Google’s new AI models are here—and here’s how you can use them…

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/94378831-3cea-4e82-a560-197bb4dbb201/Screenshot_2025-02-05_at_5.00.52_PM_1.png?t=1738813982)
Caption: 

Maybe it was in response to [the stock drop](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/02/05/alphabet-shares-fall-7percent-on-revenue-miss-heightened-ai-investments.html). Maybe it was in response to [o3-mini](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/the-new-chatgpt-o3-mini), or [R1](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/10-wild-deepseek-demos), or, more likely, both. It could have even been planned well in advance. 

Whatever the reason, Google launched its [new AI models](https://blog.google/technology/google-deepmind/gemini-model-updates-february-2025/) yesterday, which we’ll affectionately call “Gemini 2.0 (_but _[_for real this time_](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/google-meta-apple-new-ai)).” 

**The lineup includes ****[three new Gemini models](https://blog.google/technology/google-deepmind/gemini-model-updates-february-2025/)****:**

* [**Gemini 2.0 Flash**](https://aistudio.google.com/prompts/new_chat?model=gemini-2.0-flash): The “workhorse model”, now generally available.

* [**Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite**](https://aistudio.google.com/prompts/new_chat?model=gemini-2.0-flash-lite-Preview-02-05): A new budget-friendly option that makes AI more accessible.

* [**Gemini 2.0 Pro**](https://aistudio.google.com/prompts/new_chat?model=gemini-2.0-pro-exp-02-05): Google’s “most powerful model yet”, perfect for coding and complex tasks.

The standout updates? Better performance at [lower costs](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/gemini-2-family-expands/) (they eliminated the pricing difference between short and long prompts), plus some serious technical upgrades:

* A massive 2-million token context window for 2.0 Pro. 

* Built-in tool use (like Google Search integration).

* Multimodal capabilities for understanding images, video, and audio.

Google’s [experimental “thinking” model](https://deepmind.google/technologies/gemini/flash-thinking/) apparently got an upgrade too, scoring 73.3% on AIME (a notoriously difficult math competition) and 74.2% on GPQA Diamond (complex science questions).

**To actually use these models, you have multiple choices**: 

* Use the [Gemini app](https://gemini.google.com/app).

* Use [Google AI studio](https://aistudio.google.com/prompts/new_chat?model=gemini-2.0-flash-lite-Preview-02-05). 

Why are there two options? _Because… why not? _The thinking probably is Gemini = the normie app and AI studio = for the nerds. 

**Where this is all headed: **Google search [becoming an agent](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/04/google-wants-search-to-be-more-like-an-ai-assistant-in-2025/) instead of a platform. That’s right—on yesterday's earnings call, CEO Sundar Pichai laid out Google’s vision for 2025 as “one of the biggest years for search innovation yet.” Think less “ten blue links” and more “AI assistant that browses the web for you.” 

The plan includes three major initiatives:

* [Deep Research](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/new-best-ai-tool-really): An AI agent that creates detailed research reports, automating what people typically do manually with Search (here now). 

* [Project Mariner](https://deepmind.google/technologies/project-mariner/): A system that can navigate websites for users, potentially changing how we interact with the web entirely (like [OpenAI’s Operator](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/openai-s-agent-is-live)).

* [Project Astra](https://deepmind.google/technologies/project-astra/): Google’s multimodal AI that can process live video and answer questions in real-time (potentially powering AR glasses someday).

And Google knows it needs to move fast—one, so it doesn’t kill its search business without a good backup, and two, so it doesn’t lose anymore key talent. 

Just look at [NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com/): despite being one of Google's most successful AI products, Microsoft just managed to [poach the team](https://www.ft.com/content/51bb0496-59ab-4a75-a410-14c097104594) behind its popular “Audio Overview” feature (the [DIY AI podcast one](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/notebooklm-next-big-thing)). Some of these same folks also worked on Project Astra. _Ouch._ 

**This obviously has massive implications for businesses that rely on SEO**. If (_more like when*_) bots do all the searching, any added time spent clicking on extra links will literally cost users money. Making info easy to find fast (i.e., _bot-friendly_) could be key.
